$schema_note: Structured unit rates extracted ONLY from data/vendors.json paid_from / pricing_model / free_tier / oss_self_host. Null = not stated in dataset — engine must say so. Rebuild after edits.
disclaimer: All figures are estimates modeled from public pricing page text captured by O11y Watch. They are not quotes, invoices, or negotiated rates. Verify on each vendor's current pricing page before buying. Self-host software license may be $0 where stated; compute, storage, and ops labor are outside this dataset.

datadog.name: Datadog

products.note: All annual list prices from datadoghq.com/pricing/list (Billed Annually column) + allotments from datadoghq.com/pricing FAQs, read 2026-10-31.

free.note: Free tier: up to five Basic hosts with 1-day metric retention (datadoghq.com/pricing, re-read 2026-10-31). A separate plan, not 5 free Pro hosts, so never deducted from paid Infrastructure Pro hosts.

notes: Infrastructure Pro $15/host/mo annual ($18 on-demand). Every monitored host is billed; the Free tier (up to 5 Basic hosts, 1-day retention) is a separate plan (datadoghq.com/pricing, read 2026-10-31).

APM $31 per APM host/mo annual ($36 on-demand); each APM host includes 150 GB ingested spans and 1M indexed spans (15-day) per month; extra ingested spans $0.10/GB, extra indexed spans $1.70/M (15-day), $1.27/M (7-day), $2.50/M (30-day).
Logs: ingestion $0.10/GB; indexed log events per 1M: $1.06 (3-day), $1.27 (7-day), $1.70 (15-day), $2.50 (30-day) retention.
Custom metrics $5 per 100/mo beyond 100 per Infrastructure Pro host. Container Monitoring $1/container/mo beyond 5 per Pro host. These products are billed per host / GB / event, not per user.
Source: datadoghq.com/pricing/list, Billed Annually column, read 2026-10-31.

newrelic.name: New Relic
notes: Full platform users by edition (newrelic.com/pricing, checked 2026-10-31): Free = 1 full user; Standard = $10 first + $99 each additional, max 5 full users; Pro = $349/full user/mo on annual commitment ($418.80 monthly pay-as-you-go). Core users $49/user; basic users free.
Data: 100 GB/mo free, then $0.40/GB (original data) or $0.60/GB (Data Plus).
Dataset does not separate logs vs metrics vs traces GB — modeled as combined ingest GB/mo.

grafana.name: Grafana Cloud

logs.parts: Process $0.05 + Write $0.40 + Retain $0.10 per GB (each 'starts at'); we apply all three to every ingested GB, the list-price ceiling

traces.parts: Process $0.05 + Write $0.40 + Retain $0.10 per GB (each 'starts at'); all three applied to every ingested GB

notes: grafana.com/pricing read 2026-10-31: Pro $19/mo platform fee + usage. Metrics from $6.50/1k active series (10k included). Logs and traces each: Process $0.05/GB + Write $0.40/GB + Retain $0.10/GB, 50 GB included, 30-day retention. Application Observability $0.025/host hour ($18/host). Grafana users $8/active user/mo after 3 included (Enterprise-plugin users $55, IRM users $20, not modeled).
We charge Process + Write + Retain on every ingested GB, the list-price ceiling (Write applies only to data kept after Adaptive Logs/Traces, so real bills can be lower). Volume discounts not applied.

signoz.name: SigNoz Cloud
notes: signoz.io/pricing read 2026-10-31: Teams $49/mo including $49 of usage; then logs $0.30/GB, traces $0.30/GB (15-day retention), metrics $0.10 per million samples. 'No user-based pricing. No host-based pricing.'

uptrace.name: Uptrace
notes: uptrace.dev/pricing read 2026-10-31: '50 GB free/mo, then $0.075/GB' and 'Rates start at $0.10/GB and drop to $0.016/GB at scale' both appear; we use the higher $0.10/GB. Metrics from $0.025 per 1M datapoints. Unlimited users, services and hosts. 28-day default retention.

coralogix.name: Coralogix
notes: coralogix.com/pricing read 2026-10-31: logs $0.42/GB, traces $0.16/GB, metrics $0.06/GB where '1GB = 750 active time series'. 'Unlimited users included free', 'Unlimited hosts'. Data stored in your own bucket (your cloud storage bill is separate, ~$0.003/GB effective per Coralogix).

dash0.name: Dash0
notes: $0.060 per million spans/logs (ingestion).

splunk.name: Splunk Observability Cloud
notes: splunk.com observability pricing read 2026-10-31: Infrastructure from $15/host/mo, App & Infra (APM) from $60/host/mo, End-to-End from $75/host/mo, billed annually. Logs come via Log Observer Connect (your Splunk Platform license, priced separately, no public per-GB rate), so log volume cannot be priced.

dynatrace.name: Dynatrace

foundation.label: Foundation & Discovery
foundation.scope: basic infrastructure monitoring and IT inventory only, not APM

infrastructure.label: Infrastructure Monitoring
infrastructure.scope: infrastructure observability (process, disk, memory, network, custom metrics), not APM

fullstack.label: Full-Stack Monitoring
fullstack.scope: APM + infrastructure; includes a trace allowance (size not stated on the pricing page)

notes: Tier matches what you replace (dynatrace.com/pricing, checked 2026-10-31): APM/full-stack → Full-Stack Monitoring $58/mo per 8 GiB host (billed $0.01 per memory-GiB-hour, so larger hosts cost proportionally more); infrastructure-only → Infrastructure Monitoring $29/mo per host ($0.04/host/hour). Foundation & Discovery ($7/mo per host) is basic infrastructure only and is never used for APM.

Rates are rate-card prices drawn down from a Dynatrace Platform Subscription (DPS): a minimum annual spend commitment; unit prices fall as the commit grows; usage above the commit is billed monthly at the same rates.
Unlimited seats (no per-user fees). Log, trace-overage, RUM and other product rates are not modeled.

Rate card read 2026-10-31 (dynatrace.com/pricing/rate-card): Log Ingest & Process $0.20/GiB + Retain $0.0007/GiB-day; Metrics Ingest & Process $0.15 per 100k datapoints; Traces ingest included with Full-Stack Monitoring (allowance size not stated), extra $0.20/GiB. We treat survey GB as GiB (overstates by ~7%).

honeycomb.name: Honeycomb
notes: Pro from $150/mo; event volume tiers — overage unit rates not in dataset. Modeled as Pro floor when above free tier.

axiom.name: Axiom
notes: Paid from $25/mo; limits are compute units not GB of logs — cannot map usage GB to dollars from dataset alone. Teaser uses paid_from floor only when free allowance likely exceeded.

middleware.name: Middleware
notes: middleware.io/pricing (re-read 2026-10-31): Pay As You Go is $0.3 per GB of metrics, logs and traces. Data volume is the sum of uncompressed logs, metrics and traces, measured daily (10 GB/day = 300 GB/month). Free Forever includes 100 GB data/month, 14-day retention and unlimited users; Pay As You Go has 30-day default retention.

Middleware publishes no per-host fee, no per-span or per-series rate, and no bytes-per-span factor, so host, span and series counts are not converted to GB. With spans or custom metrics but no GB volume for them, Middleware is listed as insufficient data rather than priced.
RUM $1 per 1K sessions, synthetics $1 per 5K checks and browser tests $10 per 1K runs are published but not modeled (the survey does not collect them).

openobserve.name: OpenObserve
notes: Cloud: $0.50/GB ingested + $0.01/GB queried. Query volume not collected in survey — ingest only modeled; query line marked unknown.

observe.name: Observe
notes: $0.49/GiB logs; per-DPM metrics rate not captured — metrics dimension unknown.

groundcover.name: groundcover

levers.name: Retention reduction
levers.description: Lower log/metric retention toward free-tier or 14–30 day defaults where vendors publish them.

levers.name: Trace/span sampling
levers.description: Sample high-cardinality traces (e.g. 10–25% keep) when span volume drives cost.

levers.name: Log volume filters
levers.description: Drop debug/verbose and high-chatter sources before ingest.

levers.name: Seat / user rationalization
levers.description: Move viewers to basic/read-only seats where the vendor distinguishes full vs basic users (e.g. New Relic).

span_bytes.quote: An average span is about 500 bytes plus custom attributes
span_bytes.use: Only when the buyer gives span COUNT but not trace GB, to estimate GB for vendors that bill traces by GB. Always an assumption (confidence capped at Medium); real spans with attributes are larger, so trace cost is likely understated.

datapoints_per_series_mo.quote: Typically, each timeseries produces one datapoint per minute ... collection_interval / scrape_interval both default to 1 minute
datapoints_per_series_mo.use: Active series x 60 x 24 x 30 for vendors that bill metric datapoints/samples. Always an assumption (confidence capped at Medium); a 30s interval doubles it.
